title: Install picked design packs at onboard, prune the rest, and offer the pick
action:
RED FIRST: write the failing tests before the code, in onboard/tests.rs (sandbox host; copy `fn a_fresh_apply_writes_the_pi_table_and_records_the_offer() {` at tests.rs:208 and its CRLF sibling) and in the skills.rs unit tests (copy `fresh_target_plans_one_sync_per_source_skill`), and watch each fail for its own reason.

(1) SOURCE (per D4 and the packaging decision). The taste lives in packages/bee/design/ as six ready-made skill dirs: bee-design (core) and bee-design-web, bee-design-charts, bee-design-motion, bee-design-apple, bee-design-figma. Add a design source root to the onboard Engine (source.rs, beside `skills_root: plugin_root.join("skills"),`): <plugin_root>/packages/bee/design. In skills.rs `pub fn compute_skill_items(source_root: &Path, target_root: &Path, runtime: &str) -> Vec<Value> {` both the source listing (`let source_entries = list_bee_skill_entries(source_root);`) and the prune loop (`for entry in list_bee_skill_entries(target_root) {` at :222) decide names. Make the source domain = skills/ bee-* entries PLUS, from the design root, `bee-design` and each `bee-design-<pack>` whose pack is in the host's pick; `bee-design` is included whenever at least one pack is picked. Each item records its own source dir, and the two apply arms (apply.rs, the `sync_skill` and `remove_skill` arms that today re-read skill_sync.source_root) use the item's own source. A target bee-design* dir not in the domain is pruned exactly like any other absent bee- skill; non-bee dirs stay untouchable. Do not move or rename anything under packages/bee/design/ or skills/.

(2) PICK. Host .bee/config.json key `design.packs`: an array of pack names from {web, charts, motion, apple, figma}, or the string "none". Add `--design-packs <comma list|none>` to the onboard Args struct (mod.rs `struct Args {`) and parse_args, thread it into Options, and in apply write design.packs into the host config only when it changes, keeping indent unit and CRLF exactly as `fn add_pi_team` (apply.rs:854) does. An unknown pack name refuses before any write, naming the valid names. `--design-packs` with no `--apply` reports the planned write only.

(3) OFFER. Add a DESIGN_PACKS_OFFER constant in templates.rs beside NO_TEST_VERIFICATION_OFFER, in plain language (no config path, key name or bee term): it says the project has UI files, lists the five packs with one line each on the project type it serves, says how to pick (the agent runs onboard with the chosen packs, or none), and warns that bee replaces edits inside its design folders on every install. In notices.rs `pub fn stale_advisor_notices(repo_root: &Path) -> Vec<String> {` push it when the host config has no design.packs key AND a bounded scan finds a UI file (.html .css .scss .jsx .tsx .vue .svelte; skip node_modules, .git, target, dist; stop at the first hit and at a depth/file cap). No offer when design.packs is set, including "none". The offer never writes anything.

(4) UPGRADED HOSTS (per D3). In apply, add team.<runtime>.design to an existing host config when absent, from the seeded defaults (templates.rs default_config), the same only-if-absent way the pi table is added at apply.rs:863, and stamp a ledger key in .bee/onboarding.json (mirror PI_TEAM_OFFERED_KEY) so a user who deletes the row does not get it back.

Tests (sandbox host unless noted): --design-packs web,charts --apply writes exactly bee-design, bee-design-web, bee-design-charts into .claude/skills (and the other repo skill homes) and records design.packs; a second apply with --design-packs web removes bee-design-charts and keeps a host skill named my-design; a host with no pick gets no bee-design* dir; --design-packs none removes every bee-design* dir; an unknown pack refuses with no write; a host with an index.html and no pick gets the offer, a host with design.packs set or no UI file does not; an existing CRLF 4-space config gains team.claude.design and keeps its other bytes; deleting the design row then re-applying does not re-add it; the existing skills sync unit tests stay green.
